questions.prompt: Can a corporation give unlimited money to a super PAC?
questions.why: Since Citizens United and SpeechNow.org (2010), corporations, unions and individuals can give super PACs unlimited sums.

questions.prompt: CLF (a super PAC) has spent $3.2M in WI's 1st District House race. Which party is it helping?
questions.why: Its spending supports the Republican or attacks their opponent. Every group's filings list who it backs or opposes.

questions.prompt: A party's coordinated spending in the last three weeks before Nov. 3 is disclosed when?
questions.why: Coordinated spending appears only on regular reports. Anything after Oct. 14 lands on the post-general report, due Dec. 3.

questions.prompt: A hybrid PAC can do what a super PAC can't. What?
options: Give directly to candidates from a limited account
questions.why: A hybrid PAC keeps two accounts: a limited one for contributions to candidates and an unlimited one for independent spending.

questions.prompt: Groups helping Democrats have spent $684K in CA's 34th District House race. Are Democrats playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Democrats hold this seat now, so money helping Democrats here is defense.

questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
Groups helping Republicans have spent $9.9M in IA's 2nd District House race. Are Republicans playing offense or defense?
questions.why: Republicans hold this seat now, so money helping Republicans here is defense.

questions.prompt: Which race has drawn more outside money so far in the general election?
In FL's 14th District House race, outside money favors Republicans by $6.3M. Whose nominee has raised more?
questions.why: Outside money and candidate money point opposite ways here: the Democrat leads fundraising by $2.1M.
